About This Document

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) explains how to use MEDILab's internal Operational Logistics platform to request, approve, and schedule company vehicle trips. It is written for two audiences: Requestors (any MEDILab employee who needs to send a driver somewhere) and the HR Manager (who reviews and approves all requests).

Driver-specific instructions — how to check the calendar, prepare for a trip, and report completion — are covered in a separate document: MED-LOG-002 Driver Scheduling & Trip Execution SOP.

Read this document in full before using the scheduling module for the first time. Even if some steps seem self-explanatory, understanding the entire workflow prevents errors that affect drivers, clients, and other departments.

INTROWhat Is the Operational Logistics System?

MEDILab has introduced a dedicated internal fleet management platform as part of its operational digitization initiative. Previously, driver scheduling was managed through phone calls, informal messages, or verbal arrangements — which led to double-bookings, missed trips, and no audit trail for fleet usage.

The Operational Logistics module, accessible through the MEDILab internal platform under the "Scheduling" menu, provides a single place where:

  • Any MEDILab employee can submit a formal, traceable trip request for a driver and vehicle.
  • The HR Manager can review, approve, or reject requests in a structured queue — with full visibility of the fleet calendar before deciding.
  • Drivers can see their confirmed assignments on a calendar without needing to receive calls or messages.
  • Management has a complete record of all fleet activity for accountability, planning, and cost tracking.

Why are we doing this? MEDILab operates across multiple governorates and serves hospitals, universities, and public institutions. Our drivers handle deliveries, client visits, and maintenance runs simultaneously. Without a system, it is impossible to prevent conflicts, track vehicle usage, or provide clients with reliable service windows. This platform solves that.

Figure 1 — MEDILab internal platform. Access the fleet system by clicking 'Scheduling' in the top navigation bar.
ℹ️
How to Access: Log into the MEDILab internal platform. In the top navigation bar, click "Scheduling". This opens the Operational Logistics dashboard — the starting point for all actions in this SOP.

The Dashboard at a Glance

When you open the Scheduling module, you land on the Operational Logistics dashboard. This screen shows:

  • System status (Active / Inactive) and current number of assigned drivers
  • A three-tab board tracking trip requests at each stage of their lifecycle
  • A mini calendar showing the current month with clickable dates
  • Buttons to open the full Calendar View and submit a New Trip Request
Figure 2 — The Operational Logistics dashboard. The three tabs (Approved & Scheduled, Pending, Completed/Archived) track every request. The calendar on the right gives a monthly overview. The filter icon (funnel) on each tab allows filtering by status, including Rejected.

Trip Request Lifecycle

Every trip request passes through the following stages. No trip is executed without an Approved status. The system automatically moves a trip to Completed once its scheduled date has passed.

🔄
Automatic Completion: The system automatically changes a trip's status to Completed once its scheduled date has passed. No manual action is needed from the HR Manager or driver to close out a trip.
01Purpose

This SOP defines the step-by-step procedure for submitting a vehicle trip request, having it reviewed and approved by the HR Manager, and ensuring the assigned driver's trip is visible on the scheduling calendar. It also covers what happens when a request is rejected, how completed trips are recorded automatically, and how to find rejected or past requests using the dashboard filters.

Following this procedure consistently ensures: no driver is double-booked, every trip has HR authorization, clients receive reliable service, and MEDILab maintains a complete, auditable record of all fleet activity.

02Scope

Who this applies to: All MEDILab employees and engineers who need to request a company vehicle and driver; the HR Manager who reviews and approves requests.

What is covered: All trips using MEDILab fleet vehicles — client deliveries, procurement runs, maintenance transport, inter-department logistics, and engineer field visits.

What is NOT covered: Driver-side instructions (see MED-LOG-002); maintenance job scheduling (see MED-MAINT-001); personal vehicle use; third-party courier arrangements.

📅
Advance Notice Policy: The internal policy is to submit trip requests at least 24 hours in advance. Same-day requests are not standard and will only be considered at the HR Manager's discretion on a case-by-case basis. There is no system restriction preventing same-day submission, but requestors should not assume same-day requests will be approved.

05Before You Begin — Prerequisites

Before submitting a trip request, confirm all of the following:

  • You have an active MEDILab platform account with access to the Scheduling module.
  • You have the following information ready: exact destination, trip date, required time window (start and end), vehicle type, client/end user name, and the contact person's name and phone number at the destination.
  • You have checked the Calendar View to confirm your preferred driver has no existing approved trip that overlaps your requested time window (see Step 1a below).
  • Your trip date is at least 24 hours from now. Same-day requests require HR Manager discretion and are not guaranteed approval.
  • If the trip is linked to a maintenance job, the Maintenance Job ID must already exist in the system before you submit.
PHASE ASUBMITTING A TRIP REQUEST
Purpose of this phase This phase is for the Requestor. A well-completed request gives the HR Manager everything needed to make a fast, informed decision and gives the driver everything needed to execute the trip without confusion. Incomplete or inaccurate requests will be rejected, causing delays for you and for the client.
1a
Check driver availability on the Calendar View before opening the form. Requestor
Before you submit a request, spend one minute checking that your preferred driver is actually free. This saves your request from being rejected purely due to a conflict you could have caught yourself. From the dashboard, click "Calendar View", switch to Week or Day view, navigate to your trip date, and look at your preferred driver's color column. If it is empty during your time window, they are available.
Figure 4 — Week view. Moustafa Serhan (green) has an approved trip on Thursday Apr 30 from 10:00 AM–3:30 PM. If you wanted to request Moustafa for any overlapping time on that day, you would need to choose a different driver or a different time before submitting.
1
Open the New Trip Request form. Requestor
From the Operational Logistics dashboard, click the blue "+ New Trip Request" button in the top-right corner. The trip submission form will open.
Figure 5 — The dashboard. Click '+ New Trip Request' (top-right, blue) to open the form. 'Calendar View' beside it is where you check availability first.
2
Complete all required fields in the form. Requestor
Fill in every required field carefully. Each field is explained in the reference table below. The form will not submit if required fields are empty, but it cannot check whether the information you entered is correct — that responsibility is yours.
Figure 6 — The trip request form. This example shows a completed request: Driver Moustafa Serhan, Department Procurement, Date Apr 30, Destination Zgharta, Vehicle Truck, Time 10:00–15:30, Client AUB, Contact Mr. Georges Wassouf, Note 'Take P.O. from Perla (Sales Department)'.
Select Driver REQUIRED
Choose from the 4 active drivers. Only select a driver you confirmed is available in the calendar (Step 1a).
Department REQUIRED
Your department (Procurement, Sales, Clinical, etc.). Used by HR for accountability and cost allocation.
Date of Trip REQUIRED
Select using the date picker. Should be at least 24 hours from today. Same-day only with HR Manager discretion.
Destination REQUIRED
Select from the dropdown. If your destination is missing, choose the nearest option and specify the exact location in the Notes field — then notify HR to add it.
Preferred Vehicle REQUIRED
Select based on what the trip needs (e.g., Truck for equipment delivery). HR may override if the vehicle is unavailable.
Start Time / End Time REQUIRED
Set a realistic window. Include loading time, travel time, and time at the client. This defines the block on the calendar — underestimating blocks other drivers from that slot.
End User (Client) REQUIRED
Full name of the organization or person being served. Appears on the trip card visible to HR and on the driver's calendar.
Contact Person & Number REQUIRED
Name and phone number of the person at the destination. The driver uses this to coordinate upon arrival.
Estimated Distance OPTIONAL
Approximate km (e.g., 30 km). Used to classify trip as Local / Regional for fleet cost tracking. Leave blank if unknown.
Link to Maintenance Job OPTIONAL
Link to an existing maintenance job ID if this trip is connected to one. Leave as "----------" otherwise.
Notes / Duration Details OPTIONAL — but important
Add any instructions the driver or HR must know: "Collect P.O. from Perla (Sales) before leaving", "Wait for client signature", "Urgent same-day — please review".
3
Review all entries carefully, then submit the form. Requestor
Before clicking Submit, read through every field once more. Common mistakes: wrong date, missing contact number, unrealistic end time. Once submitted, you cannot edit the request — if you made an error, you must ask the HR Manager to reject it so you can resubmit correctly.

After successful submission: the system assigns a TR-XXXX reference number and moves your request to the Pending (Require Approval) tab with status Pending Review. Make a note of your TR number for follow-up. The HR Manager will review it — you do not need to call or message unless it is a same-day or urgent request.

PHASE BHR MANAGER REVIEW & DECISION
Purpose of this phase This phase is for the HR Manager. No trip is executed without HR authorization. This review step exists to prevent double-bookings, ensure vehicle suitability, and maintain operational oversight of all MEDILab fleet movements. The HR Manager has full discretion on approval — including the ability to approve or decline same-day requests based on operational context.
4
Open the Pending (Require Approval) tab and review all waiting requests. HR Manager
From the Operational Logistics dashboard, click the "Pending (Require Approval)" tab. All submitted but unreviewed requests appear here as trip cards. Check this tab at least twice per business day — at the start of the day and after midday. Requests should not remain unreviewed for more than 4 business hours during working hours.
Figure 7 — A trip request in the Pending tab. This card shows: TR-0054, destination Zgharta, client AUB, date Apr 30, time 10:00–15:30, driver Moustafa Serhan, requested by Rawad Zeidan (Procurement), vehicle Truck, distance Local, status 'Pending Approval'.
5
Review each request for completeness and feasibility. HR Manager
For each pending card, verify the following before making a decision:
  • Driver availability: Open the Calendar View in Week or Day view. Confirm the assigned driver has no existing approved trip overlapping this time window on this date.
  • Vehicle suitability: Is the requested vehicle type appropriate? (e.g., Truck for equipment delivery is correct; a Sedan for moving heavy equipment is not.)
  • Time window realism: Does the time window make sense for the destination and task? Flag if the end time appears too short for the distance involved.
  • Advance notice: Is this a same-day or very short-notice request? If so, assess based on operational context and your discretion.
  • Notes: Read the Notes field — the Requestor may have flagged special instructions or an urgency reason.
⬡ Decision Point — After Reviewing the Request
APPROVE → All details correct, driver available, no conflict, request is operationally sound. Proceed to Step 6.
REJECT → Conflict exists, information is wrong or missing, same-day request is not feasible, or operational issue identified. Proceed to Step 7.
6
Approve the request. HR Manager
Click the Approve action on the trip card. The system immediately: changes status to Approved, moves the card to the Approved & Scheduled tab, sets the sub-status to Scheduled, and creates a color-coded calendar event visible to the assigned driver.
Figure 8 — TR-0054 after approval. Status is now 'Approved' and 'Scheduled'. The card has moved to the Approved & Scheduled tab. Moustafa Serhan can now see this trip on his calendar automatically — no phone call needed.

You do not need to notify the Requestor of an approval — they can check the Approved & Scheduled tab themselves. Drivers check the calendar independently (covered in MED-LOG-002). If there are special operational instructions not captured in the Notes, you may contact the driver directly.

7
Reject the request and call the Requestor to explain the reason. HR Manager
If the request cannot be approved, click Reject on the trip card. The status changes to Rejected. Immediately after rejecting, call the Requestor by phone to explain why the request was rejected and what they need to do to resubmit correctly. Do not leave a rejection without a phone explanation — the Requestor will not know why it was rejected otherwise.

Common rejection reasons to communicate clearly:

  • "The driver you selected already has an approved trip at that time — please choose a different driver or a different time window and resubmit."
  • "This is a same-day request and we cannot accommodate it today. Please plan 24 hours ahead and resubmit for tomorrow."
  • "The contact number is missing from the form — please resubmit with the client's phone number."
  • "A Truck is not available on that date — please request a Van instead."

After the call, the Requestor submits a new, corrected request starting from Step 1.

🔍
Finding Rejected Requests: Rejected requests remain visible in the system and are accessible by both the HR Manager and the Requestor. To view them, go to the relevant dashboard tab and use the filter icon (funnel) to filter by "Rejected" status. The request will show its TR-XXXX number and all submitted details for reference.
PHASE CAFTER APPROVAL — WHAT HAPPENS NEXT
Purpose of this phase Once a trip is approved, the process moves to the driver and the system takes over. This phase explains what the Requestor and HR Manager should expect after approval, how the calendar reflects approved trips, and how the system automatically closes trips once they are completed.
8
Confirm the approved trip appears correctly on the Calendar View. HR Manager
After approving, quickly verify that the trip block appears on the calendar in the correct driver's color, on the correct date and time. This takes 30 seconds and catches any data entry errors before the driver acts on incorrect information.
Figure 9 — Day view for April 30. The approved trip appears as a green block (Moustafa Serhan): 10:00 AM–3:30 PM, Zgharta (American University of Beirut), Truck. This is exactly what the driver will see when they check their calendar.
9
Requestor checks the Approved & Scheduled tab to confirm their request was approved. Requestor
You do not need to wait for a call to find out if your trip was approved. Simply open the dashboard and check the Approved & Scheduled tab. If your TR-XXXX appears there with status Approved and Scheduled, the trip is confirmed. If it is not there, check the Pending tab — it is still under review. If you cannot find it anywhere, check the Rejected filter (Step 7 above).
10
System automatically completes and archives the trip after the scheduled date passes. System (automatic)
Once the trip's scheduled date has passed, the platform automatically changes the status to Completed and moves the record to the Completed, Archived tab. No action is needed from HR, the Requestor, or the driver to trigger this. The archived record remains accessible for reference, audit, and fleet cost analysis.

To view past completed trips: click the "Completed, Archived" tab on the dashboard. All past trips are stored here with their full details (TR-XXXX, driver, destination, client, date, requester, department).

PHASE DCANCELLATIONS & EXCEPTIONS
Purpose of this phase Not every submitted request will proceed as planned. This phase covers what to do when a trip needs to be cancelled after approval, when a driver becomes unavailable, and other situations that fall outside the standard flow.
⚠️
Cancelling an Approved Trip: If you need to cancel a trip that has already been approved, contact the HR Manager as early as possible — ideally before the driver has started preparing. The HR Manager will update the system. Drivers check the calendar manually (see MED-LOG-002), so prompt cancellation notification is critical to avoid the driver departing for a cancelled trip.
⚠️
Driver Becomes Unavailable After Approval: If an assigned driver cannot make an approved trip (illness, emergency), the HR Manager must immediately either re-assign the trip to an available driver in the system, or contact the Requestor and the client to reschedule. Do not leave an approved trip without a confirmed, available driver.
🚫
Unauthorized Vehicle Use — Zero Tolerance: No MEDILab vehicle may be used without an approved trip request in the system. Any trip executed without an Approved status in the platform — regardless of who verbally authorized it — must be reported to the HR Manager and documented. Repeat violations are escalated per the company HR and conduct policy.
ℹ️
Destination Not in Dropdown: If your destination is not in the list, select the nearest equivalent, specify the exact location in the Notes field, and separately notify the HR Manager to add it to the system. The HR Manager should ensure new destinations are added within 2 business days.
